name: El Paso Gas Pipeline / McCloud Lateral Project

values.StartLocation: El Paso Natural Gas Lines 1100 and 1103, El Paso County
values.EndLocation: McCloud Meter Station, El Paso County
values.Owner: El Paso Natural Gas Company LLC
values.DataCenterNotes: The campus is Meta's data center in northeast El Paso, Texas, built on about 1,000 acres. A Texas Tribune article from January 2026 gives 1 GW and $1.5 billion, with groundbreaking in October 2025. An analyst post from Measured AI in 2026 gives 960 MW of computing load on 1,039 acres, about 4 million square feet, and a cost of $14.3 billion. It says a BlackRock-led venture owns 80 percent and Meta 20 percent, with Meta as tenant, and that the project was code-named Project Seafox. Power comes from the McCloud plant, a 366 MW natural gas plant that El Paso Electric would own. Measured AI says Enchanted Rock builds it and that it would run alone at 225 MW by mid-2027. Its state approval is contested, with a regulatory deadline of December 9, 2026. The same post says the gas comes from El Paso Natural Gas through a McCloud Lateral with 167,000 dekatherms per day from January 1, 2027. Measured AI says rent starts December 1, 2028. No regulator or company document read names the lateral and the campus together.

researcher_notes: EPNG filed a prior notice with the federal gas regulator on July 30, 2026 (docket CP26-558) for a lateral about 5.8 miles long and 16 inches wide in El Paso County, Texas. It would carry up to 167,000 Dth per day from EPNG's south mainline to a new McCloud Meter Station and cost $20.3 million. The notice says only that the gas goes to a planned power generation facility. It does not name a data center. A Kinder Morgan open season posted in March 2026 offers the same 167,000 Dth per day, with Enchanted Rock as the receipt point and a target start of January 1, 2027. Enchanted Rock builds the McCloud gas plant that El Paso Electric is proposing for Meta's El Paso data center, and the Texas Tribune confirms that plant exists and is meant for the data center. One analyst post (Measured AI) ties the open season to that plant directly, using El Paso Electric's filing that names Kinder Morgan as its gas supplier and a matching delivery fee. No regulator or company document names the lateral and the data center together, so the data center tie is medium confidence. Not the same as existing rows: South Mainline Expansion (P2617) is a different, finished project, and Norte Crossing (P2568) is a different line. This is a new expansion row on the El Paso Gas Pipeline. Owner spelling follows the ownership team style (El Paso Natural Gas Company LLC). The open season states a 5-mile, 16 inch lateral and the filing states 5.8 miles, so the filing figure is used. No route was found. Start year is not staged because the January 2027 date is a target only. Status is proposed because the prior notice has no approval yet.
